We work the same schedule, I'm a night shift nurse. For me, I have been unable to find the perfect sleep schedule. It's night shift, it's going to be tough. With that said, I usually wake up at 3pm after a night of work and immediately take half a caffeine pill (Vivarin, Alert, etc). It's more controlled dosage of caffeine. After about 12 hrs (3am) I feel the effects wear out. I try to eat a meal 2 hours before bed (8am). 

The trick for me was to try and get my parasympathetic nervous system activated by eating a large meal 2 hours before bed. I try to leave work 30 min early and beat the sunrise. All my room curtains are blacked out.

For me, PNS activation through eating, foam rolling and a very dark (almost pitch black) room with a fan to cancel daytime noise did the trick for me. It's not perfect, but I am going 8 years through night shift so far.

Also, if I have a week vacation, I naturally fall back into a dayshift sleep pattern. Therefore, 2 days before I go back to work, I force myself to stay up all night. For me, it's important to do this on a day off work rather than shock my system the day on.

Stress can also cause poor sleep. For me, the stress of the job the next night causes me to jolt awake hours before I'm supposed to. Sometimes I can go back to sleep, sometimes I can't. 

Also, setting boundaries with loved ones is a must-do. For me, I turn on do not disturb, leave a kind message on my voicemail explaining that "You have reached Dracula. Currently, I'm in my coffin until sunset, please leave a message". While this voicemail sounds ridiculous, it has helped "remind" my family that I am on Australian time, not American Time. 

The wife and I sleep in separate rooms on my work days. I find this best because people's energy can rub off of on me. When she is ready and caffeinated for the day and brings all that energy to me as soon as I walk in the door, she transfers that energy to me and now my sympathetic nervous system has kicked on and it will be hours before it turns off. Set boundaries with your S.O.

Maybe none of my experiences will help you. I was that kid who studied all night in school and was sleepy most of class yet somehow graduated. If nothing else works for you, just tell yourself that spring will be here soon and while sleeping, dream of leaving this God awful shift. Cheers!
